video.title: 3 Tips to Rip the Low Backhand

classification.reason: The coach provides executable cues and technical directives for ripping low backhands, including dipping the back knee, hinging at the hips with a flat back, and driving hands forward past the front foot.

problem.title_as_question: How to Rip the Low Backhand?
problem.definition: Rec players struggle to attack and drive through low backhands because they remain too upright, bend from the spine rather than hinging at the hips, and yank the racket up over the shoulder instead of extending forward.
problem.target_player: rec players struggling with low backhands

quotes.text: All right, we're going to go over three fundamentals that will help you rip the low backhand.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: The first one is this back knee, and I want you to see just how deep that is.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: We need to get this knee deep for balance purposes and so we can use it to drive through the ball.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: you can press through that knee, press that back foot through towards your target
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And this knee is out over the toe here. That is the most athletic, most efficient way to play this ball.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: A lot of rec players when they hit this shot, they're a lot straighter than they think. They might think they're bending the knee, but they are not really sitting down into this deep knee bend position
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: The second fundamental we're going to talk about is the angle of the torso.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: She's not bent over in the sense that her back is curved, but her hips are hinged, and that allows her racket path to go more low to high than usual.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: When you tilt like this, that makes your hands naturally go low to high with the same biomechanically efficient swing that you always use.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: We also have to tilt the torso, hinge at the hips, back straight. We're not bending over like curling over, but tilt the torso, hinge at the hips.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: That's how you attack these low balls and get the hands to fly up when you throw them out away from your body like you normally do.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: For our third fundamental, we're going to use the side view... So, we can see just how far out in front of her Alexa's hands are flying.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: her hands are clearing her front foot every stroke. Some strokes by a little, some strokes by a heck of a lot.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: We don't finish over our shoulder because we're yanking the racket over our shoulder. We throw the racket forward. We drive the racket forward.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And then by coincidence, it often finishes over the shoulder, but not always.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: I just want you to see in relation to the front foot just how much the hands extend through the shot, extend through this contact.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Take the hands, shove them forward, forward, forward through the ball. They should clear your front foot on it pretty much every single backhand you hit.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Yeah, that's good execution there. I probably need to practice this more when I play.
quotes.speaker: coach

symptoms.description: Player stands much straighter than they think and fails to sit into a deep knee bend on the low ball.
Player yanks the racket up over the shoulder rather than driving hands forward through contact.

causes.statement: The player fails to bend the back knee deeply, preventing balance and eliminating the ability to press through the ball toward the target.
The player does not hinge at the hips or tilt the torso with a straight back, preventing the normal swing from naturally producing a low-to-high path.
The player misinterprets the follow-through by actively yanking the racket over the shoulder instead of throwing and extending the hands forward through the shot.

angles.summary: Hinging at the hips and tilting the torso allows the hands to naturally swing low to high using the standard biomechanical motion.
Finishing over the shoulder is often a coincidental result of throwing forward, not an active yanking motion.
Alexa demonstrates hinging at the hips with a flat back rather than curling the spine over.

solutions.summary: Press through the deep back knee and drive the back foot toward your target as you hit.
solutions.external_goal: press that back foot through towards your target

solutions.summary: Tilt the torso and hinge at the hips while keeping your back straight rather than curling over.
Shove the hands forward through the ball and verify that they clear past the front foot on almost every backhand.
